idea: MineAssist-PdM: plataforma de mantenimiento predictivo explicable para activos críticos mineros que clasifica fallas de vibración y genera recomendaciones operativas en lenguaje natural para equipos de mantenimiento.
market: Global mining predictive maintenance market estimated at $3.2B in 2025, growing at 15% CAGR, driven by need to reduce unplanned downtime in critical assets like mills, crushers, and haul trucks.

solutions.name: GE Digital APM
solutions.observed_positioning: Predix-based asset performance management with mining-specific modules; strong install base, slow to add NLP explainability.

solutions.name: Siemens MindSphere PdM Apps
solutions.observed_positioning: Industrial IoT platform with predictive maintenance applications; broad integration, but mining requires customization.

solutions.name: ABB Ability Asset Performance Management
solutions.observed_positioning: Mining and minerals focus; combines APM with domain expertise, but explainability is limited to dashboards.

solutions.name: Uptake
solutions.observed_positioning: Industrial AI platform with heavy equipment OEM partnerships (e.g., Caterpillar); data science-driven, less mining-specific NLP.

solutions.name: Augury
solutions.observed_positioning: Machine health solutions with AI-driven vibration/ultrasound diagnosis and actionable natural-language recommendations; strong product-market fit in industrial, expanding to mining.

solutions.name: SparkCognition
solutions.observed_positioning: AI for heavy industry, including SparkPredict for PdM; strong on model interpretability, but NLP layer still evolving.

solutions.name: Fluke Accelix
solutions.observed_positioning: Integrated platform from a trusted test equipment brand; condition monitoring focus with basic analytics, less advanced explainability.

solutions.name: Bently Nevada System 1 (Baker Hughes)
solutions.observed_positioning: Dominant vibration monitoring hardware + software in mining; diagnostic recommendations based on rule engines, not generative NLP.

solutions.name: SKF @ptitude Analyst
solutions.observed_positioning: Vibration analysis software tied to SKF rotating machinery expertise; strong engineering base, limited AI explainability.

solutions.name: Falkonry
solutions.observed_positioning: Operational AI platform that explains time-series patterns; could be applied to mining vibration, but lacks pre-built mining models.

solutions.name: SAP Predictive Maintenance and Service
solutions.observed_positioning: Integrated with SAP ERP; used in mining for work-order management, but PdM relies on external sensor integration.

solutions.name: IBM Maximo with Watson IoT
solutions.observed_positioning: Enterprise asset management with AI add-ons; strong in MRO, but custom mining vibration models need development.

solutions.name: Manual Vibration Analysis + Spreadsheets
solutions.observed_positioning: Technicians use portable analyzers and Excel to track vibration data; low cost, high effort, no real-time explainability.

solutions.name: Run-to-Failure Maintenance
solutions.observed_positioning: Reactive maintenance approach still prevalent in many mining operations; high cost of unplanned downtime is accepted.

solutions.name: Immersive Technologies
solutions.observed_positioning: Mining equipment simulators with performance analytics; could evolve into maintenance advisory, but currently focused on operator training.

research_summary: The mining predictive maintenance market is crowded with both incumbent industrial giants and AI-native startups. Many competitors offer vibration-based diagnostics, but few provide truly explainable natural-language recommendations tailored to mining workflows. The threat from pure-play PdM startups with strong NLP capabilities (e.g., Augury) is high, while incumbents are slower to adopt explainability features.

competitor_signals.sourcing_brief: Heavily funded pure-play PdM with strong NLP outputs; direct threat to explainable recommendation.
Broad industrial AI platform with heavy equipment OEM ties; may lack mining-specific vibration explainability.
Incumbent APM with deep mining install base; slow to adopt explainable AI, but updates could close gap.
Cutting-edge AI applied to heavy industry; well-funded and technically sophisticated, explainability features evolving.
Dominant vibration hardware provider; software evolves slowly, but trusted in mining for decades.
